title: Dot product
starter:
%a   = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=0
%b   = buffer 4 dtype=i32 slot=1
%out = buffer 1 dtype=i32 slot=2
hints: Use the accumulator from this lesson. The only new part is what you add on each pass: `a[k] * b[k]`.
Inside the loop you need two views, `shrink %a %k []` and `shrink %b %k []`, a load of each, a `mul`, then load the accumulator, `add`, and store back into the same view.
After `%e = end %s %k` write `%acc1 = after %acc %e`, cut a view from `%acc1`, load it and store it into `shrink %out 0 []`. Finish with `after %out` and that last store.
explain: A one-element `alloc` holds the running total and starts at 0. Each pass loads `a[k]` and `b[k]`, multiplies them, and adds the product to the accumulator through the same view it loads from. The total is read through a view of `%acc1`, the version after the loop, and stored into `out[0]`, so junk in `out` never matters. Products and sums wrap like any i32.
